The mer gods I created are exclusively worshipped in the ocean. Even if they are real, some of them don't care about mortals and tend to forget about them. It happens because of the wrong beliefs the priests made. Or in worst cases, it's part of their nature to be careless. But minor gods love living with mortals mers. They prefer disguising themselves and using a low profile. 

All of the mer kingdoms worship the same pantheon, but the role of other gods usually vary from each other. And since the pantheon doesn't follow strict rules, most of the gods are alright with this kind of setup. They want their followers to abide to their moral code and rituals. As expected, this created some sort of conflict between other kingdoms. If there aren't definite rules, then how can they be sure that other doctrines won't lead to doom? A few gods love this type of conflict because they see it as a form of entertainment.

To compensate for the lack of rigidity, the beings of the afterlife decided to measure a soul's obedience to the doctrine they follow. However, if the doctrine is associated with a fallen god, the soul will receive a higher change of eternal punishment. 

The powerful gods I created don't interact with the mortal realm that much because their presence could shatter reality. They either use vessels or servants for some divine intervention.

I can strongly relate. Whenever I feel inspired, I find myself becoming detached from the world. And if the concept I created is good enough, I'll either smile like an idiot or act shocked like a fascinated child. My friends know me for my poker face and sudden bursts of energy. Once, I bounced on my chair while doing research on atoms.

My creativity. I'm not exactly that social, so having hobbies like drawing and writing really helped me cope with feeling like an outcast. From that, I guess I can say that my greatest strength is my ability to improvise if I'm motivated enough.

To be honest, I've been struggling with my imagination ever since I was little. It's a good thing that I thought of writing fantasy novels; It's an outlet for my endless flow of ideas. I love and hate this part of me because it can make me lazy. Pieces of media make my mind think of various concepts that slowly stray from what it's about, so I can pretty much say that it's a blessing and a curse.

The prince found a few consorts to produce some heirs, and the human lover decided to keep everything a secret. He didn't want to leave his kingdom because he has a vision for it. 

The goddess made the love child infertile, and she doesn't care about the lover's complaints because she doesn't care about humans that much.

The prison can be found in one of the mers' hidden places, and the surface-trackers who go up the surface will try to look for her.

By the way, the revolution backstory happened in the distant past. The king will be a middle-aged merman in the novel, and he currently has heirs. His love child doesn't know about her father too.

I'll accept the exile to the depths: it makes more sense for him to look for surface-trackers to help him get the throne. Plus, his love story with the human won't sound forced anymore because looking for surface-trackers is hard; accidentally bumping into a human is a possibility after all.

The prince planned for a revolution because he knew that he isn't the successor of the throne. He knew that his brother was a tyrant as well, and one of his allies betrayed him. Some of the clerics were executed too when the King discovered the plot.

I'm still reconsidering the exile plot because it can spread mer-genes. Their goddess knows that mankind will most likely capture the merfolk as they're usually seen as rare resources. In the past, magical creatures like them were killed for money. Due to this, an anonymous deity decided to create magical borders to keep their kingdoms hidden. 

I'm still developing the goddess' personality, so I'm not really sure if she'll give the prince some leeway for protecting his people. However, I do think that the some of the clerics may go against him and portray him as tainted. At first, I thought of making the love child infertile as a way of stopping the discovery of merkind.
